name: Guild socialism
summary: Guild socialism is the early twentieth-century British programme of workers' control of industry through democratic national guilds built on the trade unions, replacing the wage system and private capitalist ownership. It rejects bureaucratic state socialism, and proposes functional democracy in which producers run production while consumers, cooperatives and a communal body represent the wider public.
scope: The mainstream of the movement as systematised by G. D. H. Cole (Self-Government in Industry, Guild Socialism Restated, National Guilds League, 1915-1920s), with S. G. Hobson's National Guilds as background. Arthur Penty's medievalist, anti-factory strand is noted but excluded as a minority. Many modern issues were never addressed, so many answers are low-confidence.

sources.usedFor: Overview of thinkers (Penty, Orage, Hobson, Cole), the state and the movement's history; also Cole's biography page for his wider outlook.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: Guildsmen sought to abolish the wage system itself and guarantee maintenance, not to tune a legal minimum; adherents would not clearly back or reject the reform.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Cole treats production for profit and the labour-as-commodity wage system as the evil, and sets prices through guild-cooperative negotiation toward a just price instead of free markets.

public-ownership.rationale: Guildsmen favoured nationalising railways, mines and similar industries, but only with a large measure of democratic control; the state owns while guilds run them.

unions-good.rationale: Cole holds that trade unions are the main vehicle of change and should grow from brakes on management into bodies that take over discipline, hiring and control of industry.

property-fundamental.rationale: Guildsmen want means of production, distribution and exchange moved from private hands to communal ownership, so private property in them is not a fundamental right.

regulate-corporations.rationale: The aim is to replace capitalist firms with self-governing guilds rather than regulate them, so tighter regulation is neither the goal nor opposed.

worker-ownership.rationale: Guilds give workers democratic control of industry, though formal ownership rests with the community or state; control rather than title is the point, so agreement is moderate.

strong-leader.rationale: Cole's functional democracy spreads power and responsibility widely and attacks the omnicompetent state and bureaucracy, the opposite of a leader bypassing institutions.

state-harmful.rationale: Cole criticises the omnicompetent capitalist state but keeps a Commune for civic functions, so the state is reshaped rather than called unnecessary.

empower-police-military.rationale: Moved (statement review, 2026-11-11) to police-more-powers: its rationale is about police powers, and this statement now asks only about military spending.

reviewHistory.rationale: Wards would appoint and control the police and the army would be a part-time citizen force, implying democratic local control rather than more authority.
reviewHistory.author: claude-sonnet-5-5

reviewHistory.rationale: Moved (statement review, 2026-11-11) to police-more-powers: its rationale is about police powers, and this statement now asks only about military spending.
reviewHistory.author: claude-opus-5-5

decide-locally.rationale: Cole's Commune includes Wards that appoint and control police, and power is spread among functional and local bodies, but guilds are national so decentralisation is partial.

rehabilitation.rationale: Cole discusses courts and police structure but not penal philosophy, and the preference for minimal coercion gives only a weak lean.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Penty's medievalism valued inherited craft culture, but Cole's wing was not nationalist; the movement is split and largely silent.

gradual-change.rationale: Cole advocates encroaching control step by step yet calls a revolutionary element unavoidable and rejects respect for established institutions as a limit, so it is genuinely split.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Cole's excerpted text leaves foreign relations to the Commune and guilds and names no international body.

nation-first.rationale: Foreign relations are barely developed and the movement is neither nationalist nor clearly internationalist.

limit-growth.rationale: Penty and Morris-influenced guildsmen distrusted industrial expansion for its own sake, but Cole's wing wanted efficient industry; weak inference.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: Penty opposed factory production while Cole accepted modern industry; adherents split.

revolution-justified.rationale: Cole says a revolutionary element is unavoidable for thorough change and that change comes with or without violence, though coercion is a last resort.

experts-over-public.rationale: Functional democracy gives control to those doing the work and consumers a voice, not to outside experts, though teachers and professionals get self-governing roles.

central-planning.rationale: Guildsmen attack state socialism and bureaucratic control and prefer negotiation between guilds, cooperatives and the Commune over a single central plan.

socialized-markets.rationale: Guilds and the Cooperative Society negotiate prices toward a just price and guilds trade, so exchange survives under communal ownership, though not a competitive market.

land-value-tax.rationale: Cole wants rent moved to communal appropriation, but a single land tax replacing other taxes is a different scheme.

basic-income.rationale: Maintenance is tied to membership in a guild and service to the community, not an unconditional payment, though the guarantee is generous.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Foreign trade handled by guilds could be protective, but the sources state nothing on tariffs.

state-directs-investment.rationale: Credit and investment would be set by the Commune within limits guilds must follow, but the Commune is a functional democratic body, not the state, so it is a mixed case.

widespread-small-property.rationale: Cole permits small farms alongside guilds but wants the means of production communally owned rather than spread among small owners.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: The stated aim is the abolition of the wage system, replaced by guild maintenance, but money and salaries persist in guild budgets, so only the wage-labour relation is abolished.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: Cole puts credit issue, banking and currency under communal control, the opposite of leaving money to the market.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: Nulled (statement review, 2026-11-11): its rationale is about price setting, and the statement now asks only about setting wages.

reviewHistory.rationale: Guilds and the cooperative society negotiate prices under the Commune, which resembles state-recognised bargaining bodies, yet Cole's guilds are democratic and run by workers rather than imposed from above.
reviewHistory.author: claude-sonnet-5-5

reviewHistory.rationale: Nulled (statement review, 2026-11-11): its rationale is about price setting, and the statement now asks only about setting wages.
reviewHistory.author: claude-opus-5-5

one-party-rule.rationale: Cole's functional democracy rejects concentrated rule and the guildsmen oppose bureaucratic control, so a single leading party is contrary to the scheme.

democracy-best.rationale: Democracy is the central theme for Cole, who wants it extended into industry, though he denies parliamentary universal suffrage is real democracy.

direct-votes.rationale: Cole criticises indiscriminate mass voting and wants representation by function, so direct votes on all laws are not his mode.

workers-councils.rationale: Cole puts power in functional bodies including guilds, consumer organisations and a Commune, not workers' councils alone, and parliament is reformed rather than replaced outright.

natural-rulers.rationale: Cole spreads power and responsibility widely and rejects rule by owners, implying no natural ruling class.

political-violence-never.rationale: Cole calls coercion a last and desperate remedy yet accepts change may come with violence and that revolution is unavoidable in part, so absolute pacifism is rejected.

war-builds-character.rationale: Cole saw war chiefly as a catalyst for worker unrest, not as ennobling; guildsmen never praise it.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Cole's Commune makes law through functional democratic bodies; scripture plays no role, though Penty's medievalism is more religious.

private-courts-defense.rationale: Cole has the Commune hold war and peace, wards appoint police and the Commune appoint judges, so these are public functions.

military-superiority.rationale: Cole hopes for a part-time citizen army under the Commune and does not aim at dominance.

ethnic-nation.rationale: Not nationalist or ethnic in orientation; the movement is a class and industrial programme.

class-struggle-history.rationale: Cole uses the Marxian materialist conception to criticise democracy and sees class conflict between possessors and dispossessed, yet he is not a Marxist and stresses economic power over a class-war theory of all history.

equal-outcomes.rationale: Guild budgets set salaries and the Commune sets incomes, with no firm equal-pay rule in the excerpted text.

civilizational-union.rationale: Nothing supports this; the movement concerned industrial self-government within existing countries.

self-interest-moral.rationale: Cole contrasts commercial morality with free communal service and wants work freed from the profit motive.

duties-before-rights.rationale: Cole joins freedom with a sense of serving the community but also guards personal liberty, so adherents are split.

nature-intrinsic-value.rationale: Environmental philosophy is absent from the guild texts; Morris's influence is only suggestive.

limit-population.rationale: Population policy is not a guild socialist concern in the sources read.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: Cole accepts modern industry and seeks to democratise it, though Penty's medievalism blamed the factory system; the mainstream disagrees.

accelerate-technology.rationale: Cole accepted modern industry while Penty resisted machinery, so the movement has no common line on disruptive technology.

restore-past-order.rationale: Penty sought to restore the medieval gild while Cole and Hobson applied the idea to modern industry, so the movement is split.

results-over-ideology.rationale: Cole argued from principles of democratic self-government rather than pragmatic results, though he favoured step-by-step methods.

direct-action.rationale: Cole describes direct action as workers using their industrial organisation to take on social functions and says political action alone cannot bring the needed economic change.

means-match-ends.rationale: Encroaching control builds workers' self-government inside the old order, so the means anticipate the guild society.

return-to-foraging.rationale: Even Penty's medievalism looked to craft guilds, not foraging.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: Guilds organise production by trade and function and Cole's functionalism assumes specialised roles.

distribute-by-need.rationale: Guild salaries and maintenance are tied to service; the excerpted text sets out no principle of distribution by need.

production-for-use.rationale: The building guilds offered to produce at cost without profit, and the just price should satisfy the community's social sense.

profit-exploitation.rationale: Cole says under the wage system labour is bought as a commodity and the surplus goes to rent, interest and profit, which is a Marxian-style exploitation account.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Guildsmen reject state socialism and concentrated rule, favouring democratic functional bodies; Cole later rejected Soviet dictatorship.

collective-farming.rationale: Cole holds that small-scale farming is compatible with socialism and farms of different sizes may coexist.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: War is treated as a catalyst of unrest, but no theory of imperialism is stated.

taxation-theft.rationale: Guildsmen want rent and surplus communally appropriated and a communal budget, so taxation is legitimate.

harm-principle.rationale: Cole wants personal conduct regulated as little as possible, mainly by opinion, but does not state Mill's rule.

individual-rights-only.rationale: Cole builds on functional associations and communal service, so rights are not only individual.

exit-over-voice.rationale: Cole's whole programme is extension of democratic voice into industry and politics.

state-as-business.rationale: Guildsmen explicitly oppose production for profit and the commercial treatment of labour, and reject the idea of citizens as customers.

positive-liberty.rationale: Cole calls for freedom as self-government in work backed by guaranteed maintenance against unemployment.

media-academia-power.rationale: The sources locate power in ownership and economic control, not in universities and media, but do not discuss them.

organic-representation.rationale: Cole argues all true and democratic representation is functional representation, through trades, consumers and local bodies rather than one parliament.

total-state.rationale: Cole attacks the omnicompetent state and bureaucratic control and divides power among guilds, consumers and communes.

national-rebirth.rationale: Not a theme of the movement.

territorial-expansion.rationale: Not a theme; foreign policy is left to Commune and guilds.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: The movement seeks democratic functional self-government, not oaths of loyalty, though Penty admired medieval order.

bound-labor.rationale: The guild aim is to free labour from commodity status and give workers self-government.

universal-morality.rationale: Cole contrasts commercial morality with communal service, but states no theory of universal moral truth.

single-common-good.rationale: Cole's theory separates producers and consumers as distinct interests that organise and negotiate separately rather than assume one common good.

diaspora-return-right.rationale: Nationality and diaspora questions are absent from the movement's industrial focus.

revive-national-language.rationale: Language policy was no part of the guild programme.

workplace-democracy.rationale: Cole's core demand is democratic control of industry by workers, with consumers and the public having their own voice in policy.

school-vouchers.rationale: Cole sees education as a civic service run by teachers with cultural councils representing the public, not a voucher market.

economic-freedom.rationale: Cole holds economic power precedes political power and that capitalist freedom is not freedom, though liberty in self-government is cherished.

rule-by-example.rationale: No evidence of this view; Cole relies on institutions and public opinion.

class-collaboration.rationale: Cole sees possessors and dispossessed as opposed classes and wants workers to take control, not partnership with employers.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: The medievalist and Morris-influenced strands valued inherited culture, and Cole assigns cultural councils to protect public interest.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: Contradicts the democratic, egalitarian principles of the movement.

state-class-instrument.rationale: Cole reports that the majority of guildsmen see the state as an executive committee for administering the affairs of the whole capitalist class, though a minority differ.

elite-replacement.rationale: A conspiracy claim with no basis in the movement.

national-mission.rationale: Not a theme of the movement.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Cole says electors have little real control over representatives, but does not claim corruption.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: Contradicts equal democratic membership in the guilds.

night-watchman-state.rationale: Cole's Commune controls credit, currency, defence, police and prices, far beyond a minimal state.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: Incompatible with the movement's egalitarian democratic commitments.

socialism-one-country.rationale: Guildsmen aimed at national transformation and did not hold that socialism needs revolution elsewhere.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: Religious personal law is not a guild socialist topic.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: Cole treats education as a civic service but gives no view on religious instruction.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: Guildsmen want to reduce the state and its bureaucratic power rather than strengthen it.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Cole's democratic theory demands that power rest on those governed, through functional representation.

trade-surplus.rationale: Foreign trade is handled by guilds, but no export aim is stated.

population-transfer.rationale: Incompatible with the movement's democratic and communal principles.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: Cole calls coercion a bad thing and a last remedy, but he does not treat all force as wrong and accepts violent change may come.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: Guild socialism replaces competitive profit-seeking with cooperative communal service and just prices.

freedom-as-non-domination.rationale: Cole's demand that workers not be bought as a commodity under an employer's rule matches freedom as independence from arbitrary power, though he does not use that language.

separated-powers.rationale: Cole divides power among guilds, consumer councils and a Commune with a constitutional committee and self-governing legal profession, which checks power, though not in liberal form.

vanguard-party.rationale: Guildsmen see trade union and industrial organisation of workers as the vehicle of change, not a disciplined revolutionary party.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: Cole wants unions to grow more powerful and take over control of industry, and uses their monopoly of labour as the lever.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: Cole attributes poverty to the wage system and private appropriation of surplus.

offices-by-lottery.rationale: Cole uses functional representation and election through functional bodies, and lottery is not mentioned.

price-controls-essentials.rationale: Guilds and the cooperative society negotiate just prices, and the Commune can sell goods above or below cost for social reasons.

party-controls-media.rationale: Opposed to bureaucratic and political control in industry and to concentrated power.

party-commands-army.rationale: Cole puts armed forces under the Commune, hopes for a part-time citizen army, and does not give a party command.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: Cole distrusts representatives but does not set a rule on party discipline.

head-commands-forces.rationale: Cole places war and peace and armed forces in the Commune, not a single head of state.

clerical-rule.rationale: Cole's constitution rests on functional democracy, not clergy.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: Cole wants personal conduct regulated as little as possible and cultural councils to represent the public interest.

people-in-arms.rationale: Cole hopes for a part-time citizen army under the Commune, which is partly in line but not a total replacement of professionals.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: Penty and Morris-influenced guildsmen favoured craft and rural romance, while Cole did not stress it.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: Cole gives teachers a special role in education and does not disparage the educated.

constituent-assembly.rationale: Cole proposes a new constitution of Commune and guilds, but not specifically a constituent assembly.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: Cole wants self-government and liberty in work and minimal regulation of conduct.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: Cole's constitution has no directly elected head of state to judge.

central-bank-independence.rationale: Cole subordinates credit and currency to the communal Commune and its guild limits.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: Guildsmen want means of production put to communal use and rent appropriated by the community, though they do not frame it as a general theory of property.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: Cole later admired Soviet economy but rejected dictatorship; guild sources are silent.

sacred-ruler.rationale: Contradicts the democratic constitution of Cole's Commune.

flat-income-tax.rationale: Wealth is to be communally appropriated; a flat tax matches nothing in guild thinking.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: Cole sets a constitutional committee and self-governing legal structures to hold bodies to law.

mixed-constitution.rationale: Cole's constitution mixes functional bodies and a Commune, but not rule of the few and the many in the classical sense.

class-struggle-under-socialism.rationale: This Marxist-Leninist question concerns party states and not the guild model.

land-redistribution.rationale: Cole wants rent communally appropriated and allows small farms, but does not call for splitting estates among farmers.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: Not part of the movement and nationalist claims are alien to it.

women-must-cover.rationale: Contradicts the minimal regulation of personal conduct.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: Cole applies the Marxian materialist conception of history, saying economic power precedes political power, though he is not strictly Marxist.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: Cole's constitution has a constitutional committee and self-governing legal profession, so courts are not simply bound.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: Cole sees industrial action by union organisation as the lever and treats sudden seizure of power as very difficult.

public-money-creation.rationale: Cole places credit issue, banking and currency under communal control.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: Cole sees war and workers' unrest weakening capitalism and expects replacement via encroaching control.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: Contradicts the egalitarian and communal principles.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: Cole has a constitutional committee but no bill of rights is discussed.

elective-rulers.rationale: Democratic functional representation is elective, though the statement is about the political nation.

minority-veto.rationale: Cole's constitution has binding decisions of bodies and a last-resort coercion, and does not give individuals vetoes.

parliament-supreme.rationale: Cole rejects the omnicompetent Parliament and wants its sovereignty replaced by functional bodies.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: Guildsmen want rights and control for workers, not paternal duty of the wealthy.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: Cole requires active participation by workers in self-government.

ruling-class-consent.rationale: Cole stresses economic power and hunger and fear as past means of control, but not hegemony.

party-own-road.rationale: The guild movement had no international party line to deviate from.

military-guardian-role.rationale: Cole puts the army under the civil Commune.

office-by-exam.rationale: Cole uses functional election and appointment by bodies, with no mention of civil service examinations.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: Guild maintenance is collective and communal, so private savings accounts do not fit.

land-use-tenure.rationale: Cole wants communal appropriation of rent but allows small farms, so adherents would not hold use-only tenure.

budget-needs-parliament.rationale: Cole rejects parliament as it is, but the Commune controls budgets, so a functional analogue exists.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: Morris-influenced guildsmen criticised commercial morality, but the statement is not directly addressed.

job-guarantee.rationale: Guilds would provide continuous maintenance protecting workers from unemployment, which is close to a job or income guarantee.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: Cole keeps a Commune with law, though coercion is minimised.

industrial-unions.rationale: Guildsmen want unions that control an industry as a whole, with national guilds by industry replacing craft separation.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: A conspiracy theory with no basis in the movement.

local-production.rationale: Penty's craft revival leans that way but Cole's national guilds do not.

informal-organisation.rationale: Cole builds permanent unions, guilds and a Commune, not small informal groups.

religious-nation.rationale: Not part of Cole's programme, though Penty's strand is religious.

deference-to-leading-power.rationale: Tributary diplomacy is far from the movement.

personal-possessions-private.rationale: Cole wants personal conduct and property regulated as little as possible while the means of production go communal.

mixed-public-service-providers.rationale: Cole has guilds and cooperatives serving consumers under communal oversight but not private providers.

religion-illusion.rationale: Cole mentions religion respectfully in the medieval gild context and not as an illusion.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: Cole sees modern industry as the base for guilds, but capitalism as exploitative, so he is split.

cooperative-communities.rationale: Cole uses cooperative organisations and Wards, but not small communes holding property in common.

majority-settlement.rationale: No documented position; alien to the movement.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: Guildsmen reject both state socialism and capitalism and propose guilds as a third path, though they borrow from Marx.

suppress-opposition.rationale: Opposed to bureaucratic control and concentrated power; Cole wants coercion minimal.

participatory-democracy.rationale: Cole argues democracy must reach into industry and that workers need direct rights to frame rules and choose leaders in their workplaces.

left-right-obsolete.rationale: Guild socialism identified itself on the left and set itself between state socialism and capitalism, so obsolescence is not endorsed.

alienated-labor.rationale: Cole's critique of labour as a bought commodity under the wage system and call for freedom in work echo alienation, though without that term.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: Cole's authority comes from functional democratic bodies; Penty's medievalism is more religious.

social-market-economy.rationale: Cole replaces capitalist ownership with guilds and communal control, going beyond social protection of a market economy.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: Cole expects the Commune to direct armed forces, hoping for a citizen army.

interest-free-mutual-credit.rationale: Cole's communal credit system is non-profit and communal, but user-owned banks are not specified.

property-franchise.rationale: Cole demands wider democratic power, not property qualifications.

promulgated-standing-laws.rationale: Cole sets out courts and constitutional law but doesn't state this principle.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: Cole treats concentrated capitalist ownership and the wage system as the root of industrial servitude and wants power over industry spread to workers' guilds.

charity-over-state-aid.rationale: Guildsmen wanted maintenance guaranteed as a right through the abolition of the wage system and communal provision, not left to charity.

term-limits.rationale: Cole wanted elected, recallable officials but never addressed term limits; adherents have no clear stance.

income-for-work-not-ownership.rationale: The programme is the abolition of the wage system and of capitalist ownership, with industry run by those who work in it (s1, s2).

god-not-male.rationale: Guildsmen took no stand on religious language.

independent-unions.rationale: Guilds are built on democratically run trade unions that Cole wants kept free of bureaucratic state control.

socialism-needs-workers-power.rationale: Workers' control of industry through democratic guilds is the movement's core demand, on the basis that producers must rule production.

second-chamber.rationale: Cole's functional democracy proposed a communal body beside a guild congress, so more than one representative chamber; low confidence.

municipal-property.rationale: Cole has guilds run industry, with the state holding nominal ownership, rather than local communities owning it.

confederal-coordination.rationale: Cole favoured both local communes and national guilds, but the sources do not describe municipal confederations.

spiritual-nature.rationale: The movement was largely secular but had a medievalist strand; sources do not settle it.

regional-powers-revocable.rationale: The sources do not describe the powers of regions.

collective-bargaining.rationale: Guilds were to be built on the trade unions, which set pay and conditions collectively; the programme rests on organised industrial bodies, not individual contracts.

smash-state-machine.rationale: Cole's strategy was encroaching control from within and a Commune that reshapes rather than abolishes the state, not a revolutionary smashing of it.

workers-own-party.rationale: Guildsmen put industrial organisation through the unions ahead of parliamentary politics and were sceptical of the state, so a separate workers' party was not their main route.

immigrants-learn-language.rationale: The movement never discussed immigration or language policy, and its internationalist and communal strands point in different directions.

no-compulsory-union.rationale: Guild socialism made the trade unions the basis of the guilds with all workers in an industry belonging, so membership could not be optional; Cole does not discuss modern right-to-work rules.

democracy-is-procedure.rationale: Cole held that democracy needs real self-government in every association, including industry, and criticised parliamentary voting alone as unrepresentative.

defend-planned-state.rationale: Cole opposed bureaucratic state socialism and wanted workers' control of industry instead of state management.

indirect-election.rationale: Cole's functional democracy builds representation upward through guild and regional bodies chosen by delegates, rather than one direct vote on everything.

cut-consumption-tax.rationale: Guildsmen discussed credit, prices and currency but not consumption taxes; adherents have no clear position.

bypass-parties-groups.rationale: Guild Socialism Restated builds representation on functional bodies such as guilds, consumers' councils and the Commune, not on bypassing associations for a leader, so the claim runs against the core scheme.

market-under-party-rule.rationale: Cole rejected state socialism and bureaucratic control, and wanted workers' guilds rather than a party to run industry, so party leadership of a market economy runs against the programme.

police-more-powers.rationale: Wards would appoint and control the police and the army would be a part-time citizen force, implying democratic local control rather than more authority. (Moved from empower-police-military, 2026-11-11, when that statement became about military spending alone.)

missingStatements.text: Consumers, as well as producers, should have an organised voice in running each industry.
missingStatements.rationale: Cole holds that producers control internal management while organised consumers, chiefly cooperatives, represent the public interest in quality, price and policy.

missingStatements.text: Decisions on social questions should be made by bodies representing people according to their function, such as their trade, rather than by one geographically elected parliament.
missingStatements.rationale: Cole argues that all true and democratic representation is functional representation, since a single representative cannot speak for a person on every question.

missingStatements.text: Workers should gradually take control of their industry from within, step by step, before capitalist owners are dispossessed.
missingStatements.rationale: Cole's strategy of encroaching control has unions take over discipline, hiring and supervision inside the existing system.

notes: Cole's wing and Penty's medievalist wing differ on religion, machinery and the state; Cole's majority view is used. The majority of the National Guilds League saw the state as a capitalist instrument, while a minority thought it could be adapted. Britannica could not be opened and was not cited.
